newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-DODGERS' BRETT BUTLER HAS FAIRY TALE RETURN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-DODGERS' BRETT BUTLER HAS FAIRY TALE RETURN.

text.p: "Fairy tales, they do come true," Brett Butler said after his dramatic return to baseball after recovering from tonsil cancer.
The Los Angeles Dodgers centre fielder, who underwent tonsil cancer surgery on May 21, sparked the team to a 2-1 victory over the Pittsburgh Pirates.
"I felt like nothing has changed except that I'm gassed (tired)," joked Butler. "It reminded me of a playoff situation but with all the attention on me."

Butler's returned sooner than expected and he said he came back only because the Dodgers are in the middle of a pennant race. The win left them in a virtual first-place tie with the San Diego Padres in the National League West. The Dodgers are percentage points ahead of San Diego.
"Montreal lost, San Diego lost, we're in first place, that's the reason I came back," said Butler.

Leading off as usual, Butler grounded out to second in the first inning and flied to left in the third, but he slapped Francisco Cordova's 2-2 pitch into left field with two out in the fifth and received a standing ovation from the 41,509 fans in attendance.
But his best work came in the eighth.

Butler walked to start the inning and stole second as Todd Hollandworth struck out, taking third on Jason Kendall's overthrow. Mike Piazza was intentionally walked and Eric Karros lifted a sacrifice fly, scoring Butler with the tie-breaking run.
Butler had not appeared in a game since May 1.

"For me, after four months of two surgeries and radiation, to be able to come back and play, it's nothing short of a miracle," Butler told reporters before the game. "It's probably the biggest day of my career.

Butler's cancer, found during a tonsillectomy, was in just one of his 50 lymph nodes. It was extracted on May 1. Butler received 32 radiation treatments, then had to undergo a rigorous training programme to regain his playing weight and conditioning.

Butler dropped to 144 pounds (65 kg) because of sores that developed in his mouth and hindered eating. He gained 18 pounds (eight kg) in 19 days to climb back to 162 pounds (73 kg), his playing weight.
Butler is hitting .265 with seven RBI and seven stolen bases in 29 games this season. He was on the disabled list for just the second time in his 16-year career.

In his absence, Los Angeles tried Roger Cedeno in centre field, then traded with the Detroit Tigers for Chad Curtis. Curtis and Todd Hollandsworth manned Butler's customary leadoff spot in the batting order.
A career .291 hitter, Butler has 2,274 career hits and 542 stolen bases.
